title: fix(data): make val max_samples subsample follow validation_shuffle
bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #7824

## What

`val_max_samples` subsampling ran under `data.shuffle` because `RLHFDataset` reads a single `shuffle` flag from the config that both the train and val datasets share. With the default `legacy_data.yaml` (`shuffle: True`, `validation_shuffle: False`), the val subsample was random, contradicting `validation_shuffle` and breaking validation reproducibility across restarts.

`create_rl_dataset` now maps `data.validation_shuffle` onto the dataset-level `shuffle` flag when `is_train=False`, so the val subsample follows the same flag the val dataloader sampler already uses (`trainer_base.py` / `ray_trainer.py`), and `validation_shuffle=False` yields a deterministic head slice. When `validation_shuffle` is unset, behavior is unchanged (falls back to `data.shuffle`).

## How to check

New CPU test file `tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py` (5 cases: val follows validation_shuffle; train still follows shuffle; fallback when unset; seeded random subsample is reproducible; caller config not mutated).

```
pytest tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py -v  # 5 passed
ruff check && ruff format --check  # clean
```

Verified the core case fails on `main` (subsample is random: `selected 8 random samples out of 64`) and passes with this change (deterministic head slice rows 0-7).

## AI use disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

- The fix and tests were prepared with AI assistance (ZCode, GLM). I have reviewed the full diff line by line and can defend every change.
- Duplicate check done on 2026-10-08: no open PR touches `validation_shuffle` or the `create_rl_dataset` val path. The nearest PR is #7819 (same reporter, fixes the sister issue #7816 by seeding the train `max_samples` rng) — it does not wire `validation_shuffle` into the val subsample; this change is complementary, not overlapping.

title: [fsdp, model] fix: run fused LM heads through FSDP2 hooks
bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8091. With untied embeddings, FSDP2 shards `lm_head` independently, but fused forwards read its weight from the parent. This bypasses the head's unsharding, mixed precision, CPU offload and backward hooks. A two-GPU Qwen3 reproducer fails with mixed Tensor/DTensor operands (Torch), BF16/FP32 operands (Triton), or CPU weights under offload.

Run the fused projection through an FSDP-registered forward method on the existing head. The head keeps its own sharding group and ordinary logits `forward`; backend selection and label preparation remain unchanged. The dense, Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5 and GLM4V adapters share this entry point.

Related work: closed #7427 instead keeps the fused head in the root FSDP unit. Open #8004 adds an opt-in FP32 head and routes that branch through its head forward, while the default fused path still reads the weight directly. Open #5948 falls back to materialized logits for a sharded Qwen3-VL Torch head; this change retains fused computation and also fixes the default dense and other adapter paths. It does not implement #8090's Triton shape change or #7323's visual-call alignment.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FSDP+fused
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

On two RTX 5090 GPUs, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.6.1 and Liger 0.8.2:

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest -xsv --tb=short tests/special_distributed/test_fused_lm_head_fsdp2.py
# 144 passed on each rank (144 distributed cases, not 288 independent tests)
```

The matrix covers six small random model configurations, Torch/Triton/Liger, tied/untied heads, CPU offload on/off, two accumulated micro-batches per update, two updates, and no-grad inference. Outputs, all trainable gradients and updated parameters are compared with both ordinary HF logits and the same fused
